sn48.43:4.2: This establishes that the faculties and powers are the same. Yet the form used is not that of emphatic identity (which would employ repeated demonstrative pronouns), but could be translated, “the faculty of faith becomes the power of faith, the power of faith becomes the faculty of faith.”
sn48.43:6.3: The simile explains the different ways in which the stream can be considered, but exactly how this is to be applied is not spelled out. Rivers in the Ganges plain generally flow from west to east. This suggests that the two sets proceed in the same way, leading to the ocean of Nibbana. Along the way, however, they are for a short time split into north and south. The commentary explains the difference in terms of positive and negative: the faculties consolidate the positive qualities (of faith, etc.) while the powers quash the negative qualities (of doubt, etc.).
